Exercises

Problems to check your understanding of this chapter. The solutions are folded away — try them yourself first.

Medium

1Medium

In an economy with MPC c=0.75c = 0.75c=0.75, the government raises spending by 202020.

Find the multiplier and the total rise in income, and also the cumulative rise after the first three rounds.

  • The Multiplier: Spending That Echoes
Show solution

  1. The multiplier is 11−0.75=4\frac{1}{1 - 0.75} = 41−0.751​=4, so the total rise in income is 20×4=8020 \times 4 = 8020×4=80.

  2. The rounds run 202020, 151515, 11.2511.2511.25, and the first three sum to 46.2546.2546.25 — a little over half of the total 808080. The rest trickles in over later rounds, thinner each time.

Hard

2Hard

In an economy where investment is income-sensitive (I=20+0.1YI = 20 + 0.1YI=20+0.1Y, c=0.8c = 0.8c=0.8, income currently 420420420), every household cuts its spending by 666.

What happens to income and to realized saving?

  • The Paradox of Thrift: When Everyone Saves, No One Does
Show solution

  1. The multiplier is 11−0.8−0.1=10\frac{1}{1 - 0.8 - 0.1} = 101−0.8−0.11​=10, so income falls by 6×10=606 \times 10 = 606×10=60, from 420420420 to 360360360.

  2. Investment falls from 626262 to 565656, and realized saving follows it down from 727272 to 666666. The attempt to save 666 more ends with the economy saving 666 less.
